issues.title: Inconsistent date filter causes missing bookings in recurring event cancellation
issues.description: When cancelling recurring bookings with 'allRemainingBookings' flag, the code updates bookings using 'new Date()' as the time threshold but then fetches updated bookings using 'bookingToDelete.startTime'. This creates a time window mismatch where bookings between these two timestamps will be cancelled in the database but won't be included in 'allUpdatedBookings', causing workflow reminders and calendar event cleanup to be skipped for those bookings. This leads to orphaned reminders and stale calendar events that were cancelled but never properly cleaned up.

issues.title: Missing return value breaks caller's count tracking
issues.description: The 'updateMany' method in BookingRepository no longer returns the Prisma update result object which contains the count of updated records. According to the IBookingRepository interface, this method should return 'Promise<{ count: number }>', but the implementation now returns 'Promise<void>'. This breaks any calling code that depends on knowing how many bookings were updated, potentially affecting audit logging, metrics, or conditional logic that needs to verify if the update affected any records.

issues.title: Missing locale field causes translation failure in cancellation flow
issues.description: The 'userSelect' object used by UserRepository.findById (and subsequently findByIdOrThrow) no longer includes the 'locale' field. However, in handleCancelBooking.ts, the code calls 'getTranslation(organizer.locale ?? "en", "common")' which expects the locale property on the organizer object. Since locale is now undefined, the translation will always fall back to 'en' regardless of the user's actual locale preference, causing cancellation emails and notifications to be sent in the wrong language for non-English users.

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #24159 - chore: [Booking Cancellation Refactor - 2] Inject repositories and use them instead of Prisma in cancellation flow

structured_output.summary:
The PR moves the booking cancellation flow (`handleCancelBooking.ts`) from direct Prisma calls to injected repositories. It adds DI modules for attendee, booking-reference and profile repositories, extends `BookingRepository` with cancel-specific methods, wires everything through `BookingCancelService.module.ts`, and exposes the repositories to the platform API via `packages/platform/libraries/repositories.ts`. It also removes a duplicate `onBookingCancelled` call and adds three tests.

The direction is right, but the change is not mergeable as written. Three imports point at modules that do not exist in the repo, so the DI container cannot load and the code will not compile. The shared `UserRepository` select silently drops `locale`, which changes organizer-facing emails. The recurring-cancel lookup uses a different time window than before, so past instances get reported as cancelled. `BookingRepository.updateMany` also does not match its interface's return type. The new tests only assert `success` and `bookingId`, so they would pass even if the refactor dropped the attendee or reference cleanup they are named after.
structured_output.verdictRationale: Broken imports (`@calcom/prisma/prisma.module`, `@calcom/lib/server/repository/bookingReference`) will fail the build and break DI wiring. The `locale` removal and the recurring-cancel window change are behavior regressions. The `updateMany` return-type mismatch is a type error. These need fixing before merge, and the tests need real assertions on the cleanup behavior they claim to cover.

architecture.overview:
Before this PR, `BookingCancelService` (packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts) received a single `prismaClient` dependency and the exported `handler` called `prisma.*` directly for user, profile, booking, attendee and booking-reference queries. The DI container is built in `BookingCancelService.container.ts` → `BookingCancelService.module.ts`, and the platform API (apps/api/v2) wraps the same class through `BookingCancelModule`, passing in a `PrismaWriteService` client.

This PR introduces per-repository DI modules (`BookingAttendeeRepository.module.ts`, `BookingReferenceRepository.module.ts`, `Profile.module.ts`) and reuses the existing `User` and `Booking` modules. `BookingCancelService` now takes five repositories as deps. The handler reads them from `dependencies`, or falls back to constructing them from the global `prisma` when no deps are supplied. The platform API gets its own repository subclasses that bind the `PrismaWriteService` client. Most of the cancel flow now goes through `BookingRepository`, with a single select shared by the update and findMany paths.
steps: Entry point: `getBookingCancelService()` in `BookingCancelService.container.ts` loads `BookingCancelService.module.ts`, which resolves repositories from each repo's DI module and injects them into `BookingCancelService`.

The platform API (`apps/api/v2/src/lib/modules/booking-cancel.module.ts`) binds the same class using platform subclasses (`prisma-*.repository.ts`) that wrap `PrismaWriteService.prisma`, exposed via `packages/platform/libraries/repositories.ts`.

`BookingCancelService.cancelBooking` forwards its `deps` into `handler(input, dependencies)`. The handler uses the injected `userRepository`, `profileRepository`, `bookingRepository`, `bookingReferenceRepository` and `attendeeRepository` in place of the former `prisma.*` calls.

The recurring branch now calls `updateMany` followed by `findManyIncludeWorkflowRemindersAndReferences`. The single-booking branch calls `updateIncludeWorkflowRemindersAndReferences`, which shares the same select, so reminders and references come back in one query.
Check the DI module wiring first: three imports point at paths that do not exist, so the container cannot load until those are fixed.

findings.title: Imports reference modules that do not exist, breaking the build and DI wiring
findings.body:
Three new DI files import paths that are not in the repo:

- `@calcom/prisma/prisma.module` is imported in `Profile.module.ts`, `BookingReferenceRepository.module.ts` and `BookingAttendeeRepository.module.ts`. No `packages/prisma/prisma.module.ts` exists. The working equivalent is `moduleLoader` in `packages/features/di/modules/Prisma.ts`, which the existing `BookingCancelService.module.ts` used before this PR.
- `@calcom/lib/server/repository/bookingReference` is imported in `BookingReferenceRepository.module.ts`. That path does not exist. The class actually changed is in `packages/features/bookingReference/repositories/BookingReferenceRepository.ts`.

Typecheck will fail on these imports, and at runtime `BookingCancelService.module.ts` will throw as soon as it loads the container. Every caller of `getBookingCancelService()` breaks.

::diff{file="packages/features/bookings/di/BookingReferenceRepository.module.ts" lines="1-4"}

::callout{type="warning"}
I confirmed with `find` and grep that neither path exists at HEAD, so this is not a stale reading of the diff.
findings.fixPrompt: Fix the broken imports in three DI modules. In `packages/features/bookings/di/BookingReferenceRepository.module.ts` (lines 3-4), change the `BookingReferenceRepository` import to `@calcom/features/bookingReference/repositories/BookingReferenceRepository`. In that file and in `packages/features/bookings/di/BookingAttendeeRepository.module.ts` (line 4) and `packages/features/users/di/Profile.module.ts` (line 4), replace `@calcom/prisma/prisma.module` with the `moduleLoader as prismaModuleLoader` export from `@calcom/features/di/modules/Prisma`, which is the pattern `BookingCancelService.module.ts` used before this PR. Then run the typecheck for packages/features and confirm `BookingCancelService.container.ts` loads the container without throwing.

findings.title: Dropping `locale` from shared userSelect changes organizer email language
findings.body:
`UserRepository.userSelect` loses `locale: true`. `findById` and `findByIdOrThrow` both use that select, so `organizer.locale` is always `undefined` in the cancel flow.

The handler then falls back to English in two places:
- `tOrganizer = getTranslation(organizer.locale ?? "en", ...)` at line 337
- `language: { locale: organizer.locale ?? "en" }` at line 370

An organizer with a non-English locale will now receive cancellation emails and calendar text in English. Anything else that calls `UserRepository.findById` and reads `locale` is also affected. The field is still selected in other queries in that file (lines 351, 1120, 1328), so this is an accidental removal from the shared select rather than an intentional change.

::diff{file="packages/features/users/repositories/UserRepository.ts" lines="98-103"}
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/features/users/repositories/UserRepository.ts`, the `userSelect` object (around lines 98-103) no longer includes `locale: true`, which was removed in this PR. Restore `locale: true` to `userSelect` so `findById` and `findByIdOrThrow` return the organizer's locale again. The consumers in `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts` (lines 337 and 370) depend on it. Do not change those consumers. Check other callers of `userSelect` for the same dependency.

findings.title: Recurring cancel now returns past instances, not just future ones
findings.body:
The `updateMany` call in the recurring branch still uses `gte = cancelSubsequentBookings ? bookingToDelete.startTime : new Date()`. The follow-up `findManyIncludeWorkflowRemindersAndReferences` used to use `gte: new Date()`, and this PR changed it to `gte: bookingToDelete.startTime` unconditionally.

With `allRemainingBookings: true` and `cancelSubsequentBookings` unset, instances that started after `bookingToDelete.startTime` but before now are not cancelled by `updateMany`. They are still returned in `allUpdatedBookings`, so they are added to `updatedBookings` and passed to `onBulkBookingsCancelled`. Cancellation emails, webhooks and calendar deletion then run for past meetings that stayed ACCEPTED in the database.

The fix is to derive the lookup window from the same `gte` variable as the update.

::diff{file="packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts" lines="513-520"}
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts`, the recurring branch (around lines 497-520) computes `gte` once for `bookingRepository.updateMany`, then calls `findManyIncludeWorkflowRemindersAndReferences` with `startTime: { gte: bookingToDelete.startTime }` (line 517). That lookup window no longer matches the update's window. Change line 517 to use the same `gte` variable, so the findMany returns only the instances that were actually cancelled. Keep the rest of the recurring logic unchanged.

findings.title: `BookingRepository.updateMany` return type does not match its interface
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/features/bookings/repositories/BookingRepository.ts` (around lines 1502-1507), `updateMany` awaits `this.prismaClient.booking.updateMany` but does not return it. `IBookingRepository.updateMany` in `packages/lib/server/repository/dto/IBookingRepository.ts` (line 48) requires `Promise<{ count: number }>`. Return the Prisma result, and fix the indentation to match the class's other methods, which are indented two spaces. Re-run the typecheck to confirm `implements IBookingRepository` compiles.

findings.title: New cancellation tests do not check the cleanup they describe
findings.body:
Several of the new tests are named after behavior they never verify. Each one asserts only `result.success`, `result.onlyRemovedAttendee` and `result.bookingId`:

- "should cancel seated event and delete all attendees" never queries `attendee` rows, so a regression that skips `attendeeRepository.deleteManyByBookingId` would still pass.
- "should cancel all remaining recurring bookings" and "should cancel subsequent bookings" never check the status of the other instances, so the `updateMany` window and the `findMany` window are untested. That is the exact area where the regression above lives.
- "should handle booking reference cleanup" never checks that references were marked `deleted: true`.

These tests would pass with the cleanup removed entirely. They give false confidence. Each one should assert the database state after the call, for example attendee count, booking statuses and the `deleted` flag on references.

::diff{file="packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking/test/handleCancelBooking.test.ts" lines="1057-1161"}
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking/test/handleCancelBooking.test.ts`, the new tests added after line 1054 only assert `success`, `onlyRemovedAttendee` and `bookingId`. Add assertions that match each test's name. For the seated-event test, query attendee rows for the booking and expect none. For the recurring tests, read the other instances and expect the ones in the window to be CANCELLED and the ones before it to stay ACCEPTED. For the reference-cleanup test, read the booking references and expect `deleted` to be set. Use the same prisma/test helpers the existing tests in this file use to read database state.

findings.title: Silent fallback to global Prisma hides DI misconfiguration
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts`, `handler` (around lines 139-153) falls back to constructing repositories from the global `prisma` when `dependencies` is undefined. Remove the fallback so `dependencies` is required, and have the default export construct `BookingCancelService` with the DI-equivalent repos in one place. Alternatively, keep the default export but make it build deps explicitly and document it as a test-only entry point. Restore the TODO about removing the `handler` export so the transition intent stays visible. Update the test file's import if needed so tests cover the injected path.

findings.title: Unrelated formatting churn in the cancel handler and ProfileRepository
findings.body:
Some hunks only re-indent existing code and are unrelated to the refactor. In `handleCancelBooking.ts`, the `team:` block inside the `teamMembers && teamId && {` spread is dedented by two spaces. In `ProfileRepository.ts`, the `movedFromUser` spread and the `orgSlug` ternary are re-indented. These changes make `git blame` and review noisier. They should be reverted or split into a separate formatting commit.

::diff{file="packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts" lines="385-392"}
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts` (around lines 385-392), revert the indentation-only change to the `team:` block inside the `...(teamMembers && teamId && {` spread, so it matches the original. Do the same for the `movedFromUser` spread and the `orgSlug` ternary in `packages/features/profile/repositories/ProfileRepository.ts` (around lines 216-225 and 1017-1030). Keep only the functional changes in this PR.

findings.title: New attendee repository duplicates an existing one and breaks file style
findings.fixPrompt: Check `packages/features/bookings/repositories/AttendeeRepository.ts` for an existing method that deletes attendees by booking id. If it has one, delete `packages/features/bookings/repositories/PrismaBookingAttendeeRepository.ts`, point the DI module `packages/features/bookings/di/BookingAttendeeRepository.module.ts` at the existing class, and update the `Dependencies` type in `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts` (around lines 89-95) to use the interface. If it doesn't, rename the new class to fit the folder and match the double-quote and semicolon style used by its neighbours.

findings.title: Constructor-injected repositories keep static methods on the global Prisma client
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/features/bookingReference/repositories/BookingReferenceRepository.ts` (lines 17-22), the class has a constructor that stores `prismaClient` in a private field and also keeps a `deps` parameter property. Keep only one of these. Then move the static methods (for example `findDailyVideoReferenceByRoomName`) to use `this.prismaClient`, or leave them static but document that they use the global client and are not transaction-aware. Apply the same decision to `ProfileRepository` in `packages/features/profile/repositories/ProfileRepository.ts`.

findings.title: Cancel-path refactor keeps the fix for the duplicate audit event
findings.body: The previous revision triggered `bookingEventHandlerService.onBookingCancelled` twice. In this head there is only one call, at `handleCancelBooking.ts:561`, so the audit event fires once per cancellation as the PR description says.

findings.title: Consolidated workflow-reminder and reference reads into one repository method
findings.body: `BookingRepository` now has `updateIncludeWorkflowRemindersAndReferences` and `findManyIncludeWorkflowRemindersAndReferences`, which share the `referenceSelect` and `workflowReminderSelect` constants. Before, the same select was written inline in two places in the handler. The shared constants make it easier to keep the cancel-path shape in sync, and the `findFirstByUserId` select reuses `profileSelect`, which includes the `organizationId` and `username` fields the handler reads.
